hero.title: 100+ Questions for Couples to Ask Each Other
hero.description: A random question to get started right away, 120 questions sorted by theme just below, and all our lists for more specific moments: early dating, intimate questions, the future, long distance...

listes.sousTitre: Each list fits one situation, with its own questions and a few tips on when to ask them.

liste_intro: Here is the full list. Each theme has twenty-four questions, to read in order or to pick at random.

connaissance.titre: Questions to get to know each other better
connaissance.intro: Questions about what made you who you are: childhood, family, the choices that mattered. Even after years together, you often get an answer you didn't see coming!
questions: Which decision from your past changed you the most, and did you realise it at the time?
What did your parents pass on to you without ever saying it out loud?
Which compliment genuinely lands with you, and which one makes you uncomfortable?
What were you certain of at twenty that you no longer believe at all?
What are you genuinely good at that almost nobody notices?
Which childhood memory comes back to you most often, for no particular reason?
What tires you out in other people, when it seems to bother no one else?
Which friendship shaped you the most, and where is it now?
In what kind of situation do you feel most like yourself?
Which criticism stuck with you enough that you still think about it?
What would you do with your days if money stopped being part of the equation?
Which trait did you inherit and are still trying to correct?
What do people get wrong about you, more or less systematically?
Which failure turned out to be the most useful, looking back?
When was the last time you changed your mind about something that mattered?
What makes you angry, when you wish it left you cold?
Which place makes you feel better the moment you arrive?
What have you never told anyone, not out of shame, but because the moment never came?
Which quality do you admire most, and don't have?
What reassures you when everything is going wrong?
Which habit have you picked up recently, and what set it off?
If you had to describe yourself in one sentence you would never use in a job interview, what would it be?
Which skill would you love to have, without ever having taken the time to learn it?
What has changed in you since we've been together, without my noticing?

futur.titre: Questions about your plans and your future
futur.intro: Where to live, money, work, kids or no kids... These are the topics people put off, even though they're much easier to talk about while nothing has been decided yet.
questions: What does an ordinary day of our life five years from now look like, in your head?
What is the one thing you really don't want to see happen to us?
Where would you want to live if nothing kept us where we are?
What should we have done together before we turn fifty?
How do you picture us handling money in ten years?
What role do you want work to play in your life later on?
In twenty years, what would make you say we got our relationship right?
Is there a plan you set aside because of our relationship?
How present do you want our families to be in our life?
What frightens you most about growing old as a couple?
If we had to start over somewhere else tomorrow, would you go or stay?
What room do you want to leave for your friends in the years ahead?
How would you like us to make the big decisions?
What do you absolutely want to pass on to someone one day?
When would be the right moment for the next big step for us?
Is there something you expect from me that you have never actually asked for?
How do you want us to organise ourselves if one of us has to stop working?
Which habit would you like us to take up together and keep for a long time?
What should we stop putting off?
How would we know it's time to change something in our life?
Which compromise are you willing to make, and which one will you never make?
What would you want us to keep exactly as it is today?
If we had a whole year free, what would we do with it?
What do you hope people will say about us in thirty years?

intime.intro: This is about what brings you closer: gestures, words, and what's sometimes missing. Nothing crude, these are mostly questions about feelings.
questions: What makes you feel most loved day to day?
When did you feel closest to me?
What do you miss when I'm not there?
How do you know I'm not doing well, before I even say it?
What gives you the most confidence in me?
Is there a gesture you wish I made more often?
What kills your desire to be close, when it isn't tiredness?
How do you prefer to be comforted when things are hard?
What don't you dare ask me for?
Which time of day do you feel best with me?
What makes you jealous, honestly?
How did you know you really cared about me?
What has changed in our intimacy since the beginning?
Is there something I do that moves you without my knowing?
What helps you feel wanted?
When do you feel most vulnerable with me?
What would you like us to dare more of, together?
How would you like us to find each other again after an argument?
What makes you laugh about me, that I take for a flaw?
What do you need when you're tired and say nothing?
What has surprised you most about me since we met?
Is there a subject we both avoid without ever having agreed to?
What makes you want to confide in me rather than in someone else?
What would you like me to understand without having to explain it?

fun.intro: Questions to have a laugh, in the car, at dinner or on an evening when nobody has any ideas. They work really well with friends too.
questions: If we were a film, what would the title and the poster be?
What is the most ridiculous thing we have ever argued about?
Which TV character is most like you, and why does that annoy you?
Which completely useless skill would you love to master?
What is the worst outfit you have ever seen me wear?
If we swapped jobs tomorrow, how would that go?
What is your guilty pleasure that you would defend to the end?
Which song immediately makes you think of us, even if it's terrible?
If we won the lottery tonight, what would be the first stupid thing we did?
Which animal would you be, and which one would I be?
What is the most embarrassing thing you have done in public?
Which dish could you eat every day without ever tiring of it?
If we had a band, what would the style and the name be?
Which of your habits do you know perfectly well irritates me?
Which superpower would you take, knowing I would take the opposite?
What is the worst outing idea we have ever had together?
If our life were filmed, which scene would make the final cut?
What is the most harmless lie you have told me?
Which era would you have hated to live in, and why?
If you had to sell me to a stranger in three arguments, what would you say?
What is the most useless thing you have ever bought?
Which of us would last longer without a phone?
Which nickname do you absolutely never want me to use in public?
If we wrote a book about us, what would the first chapter be called?

profond.titre: Deep questions about values and life
profond.intro: Questions about what matters to you in life. They need a bit of calm, and that's often where the real differences show up.
questions: What gives your life meaning right now?
What would you have the hardest time recovering from?
What do you consider unforgivable?
Which injustice genuinely makes you angry?
What do you wish you'd had the courage to do?
What does success mean to you, in your own words?
Which value will you never negotiate?
What are you most afraid of, apart from dying?
What have you forgiven without ever forgetting?
Which received idea about couple life do you find false?
What would make you question your whole life?
Do you believe we really choose who we love?
What would you want people to remember about you?
Which person taught you the most, without meaning to?
What don't you understand about people of your own generation?
What makes you proud of yourself, and that you don't dare say?
What is the hardest thing you have had to accept?
What do you regret not having said to someone?
How do you tell that a relationship is worth saving?
What would you do if you knew you had one year left?
Which truth about yourself took you a long time to accept?
What do you expect from love, beyond the feeling?
Which line is nobody allowed to cross with you?
What do you want me to remind you of, on the days you forget it?

situations.titre: Which questions to ask as a couple, depending on the situation
situations.intro: A question that works great on a third date can fall flat after five years of living together, and the other way round too. Here are the situations that come up most often, with a few examples each time and the full list if you want more.

items.titre: To get to know each other better, even after years
items.texte: After a while you know your partner's habits by heart: how they take their coffee, their shows, the way they load the dishwasher. But you often know much less about what shaped them, their family or what's on their mind right now. For example:
exemples: Which family habit have you reproduced without realising it?
What would you like me to notice more often?
If our story were a book, which chapter would we be on?

items.texte: In the first weeks you mostly talk about facts: work, where you live, friends. That's normal. But some things are worth knowing fairly early, like how the other person takes criticism or what they want from a relationship, without it turning into a questionnaire. A few to start with:
exemples: What's your natural rhythm: going out or staying in?
What would I never guess about you?
What's a beautiful gesture, for you: words, time, small attentions?

items.texte: They're not necessarily about sex. Most of them are about what brings you closer: when your partner feels loved, the little gesture that gets to them, what they don't dare ask for. We sorted them starting with tenderness and moving slowly towards desire, so each of you can stop wherever you like. For example:
exemples: When do you feel most loved, concretely?
What's the ordinary little thing I do that gets to you?
What would you like us to do more often, without daring to ask?

items.titre: About the future and the big decisions
items.texte: Moving in, getting married or not, having kids, sharing money... People often avoid these topics because they're scared of disagreeing. And that's exactly why it's much easier to talk about them before making a big decision than after. Three examples:
exemples: City or suburbs, renting or buying: what's your ideal scenario?
A child: a dated plan, a vague desire, or an open question?
Joint account, separate accounts, or mixed: your model, and why?

items.titre: Long distance, over the phone or by text
items.texte: When you don't see each other much, calls end up sounding the same: your day, how tired you are, good night. One slightly different question is enough to get the conversation going again, and some even work better by text or on the phone than face to face. And to see where you stand, there are also questions written for long-distance couples. For example:
exemples: What did you think today without saying it to anyone?
What do we watch, each at home, at the same time?
What do we do, hour by hour, on the first day of the reunion?

items.titre: The 36 questions to fall in love
items.texte: This list comes from a psychology study run by Arthur Aron in 1997: two strangers ask each other 36 increasingly personal questions, then look into each other's eyes for four minutes. Lots of couples try it too, just to see what happens. We've put together the 36 questions from Aron's experiment with a few tips on how to ask them. For example:
exemples: What would constitute a perfect day for you?
If a crystal ball could tell you the truth about yourself, your life, the future or anything else, what would you want to know?
Your house catches fire, your loved ones and pets are safe: you can save ONE object. Which one, and why?

items.texte: People often ask us for questions to ask their boyfriend, especially when he isn't much of a talker. We gathered a hundred to get him talking a bit more than usual, from the lightest to the most serious. For example:
exemples: What do you wish people asked you more often?
What did we do at the beginning that we should do again?
How long would you survive in a horror film, honestly?

items.texte: And the other way round, we wrote 75 questions to ask your girlfriend. They're mostly about taking an interest in what she's going through right now, not just what she likes. A few examples:
exemples: What are you missing these days, without talking about it?
What's your safe place, the one you go to in your head?
If our relationship were a TV series, which one would it be?

items.titre: Before you're a couple: your crush or a girl you're getting to know
items.texte: Not everyone is looking for couple questions. When you're still at the texting stage, light questions that are easy to send and fun to answer work best. We have a list to keep the conversation going with your crush and another one to get to know a girl without it feeling like a job interview. For example:
exemples: Are you more of a four-minute voice note or a wall of text?
What's your perfect Sunday, hour by hour?
Which place in your city would you show someone first?

jeux.intro: Some questions go down much better as a game, because there's a rule and often a result at the end. Here are the games on the site that are built on questions:

items.texte: Questions for a first or second date, drawn one by one on your phone.
Each of you answers questions about the other, and you count who knows the other best.
Two choices every time, and you find out whether you agree.
"Never have I ever...", and each of you says whether you've done it. It often brings back old stories.
The couple version of the game, with truths to ask and dares to do.
Sentences to finish each on your own, then you compare.
Impossible choices to make together, which often end in a debate.
Spicier questions, for when the mood is right.

conseils.titre: How to ask these questions without it feeling like an interrogation
conseils.intro: There's no complicated method, but a few small things make the difference between a real conversation and a questionnaire.

items.titre: A few questions at a time:
items.texte: Three or four in an evening is plenty. If an answer opens up a topic, stay on it instead of moving on to the next one.
Whoever asks the question answers it afterwards, otherwise it turns into a job interview. And most of the time, hearing the other person's answer is what makes you want to share yours.

items.titre: Follow up instead of planning the next one:
items.texte: While the other person is talking, it's tempting to look for the next question. A simple "and how did you feel then?" works much better.
If a question makes someone uncomfortable, you skip it, no comment. You can always come back to it another day.
In the car, on a walk or at a restaurant, it works really well. In passing or in the middle of an argument, much less so!

seo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about couple questions

faq.q: What questions should couples ask each other?
faq.a: It mostly depends on the moment. For a fun evening, funny questions work really well, like "If we were a film, what would the title and the poster be?". To get to know each other better, go for childhood, family or what makes you proud. And when a big decision is coming up (moving in, a baby...), questions about the future are the most useful.

faq.q: How many questions should you ask in a row?
faq.a: Three or four per evening is more than enough. The goal isn't to finish the list but to have a real conversation, and one good question can easily fill a whole evening.

faq.q: Does it work long distance too?
faq.a: Yes, really well actually. You can send each other one question a day by text, or keep one for your evening call. We even have a list made specifically for phone calls and texting.

faq.q: What if a question makes someone uncomfortable?
faq.a: Just skip it. Nobody has to answer everything, and pushing quickly turns the game into an exam. You can always come back to it another day, when the other person is ready.

faq.q: How is this different from the 36 questions to fall in love?
faq.a: The 36 questions come from a psychology experiment: two people ask them in order, without skipping any, in about an hour and a half. Our 120 questions can be picked freely, in any order, and they're written for people who are already together.

faq.q: Can these questions replace couples therapy?
faq.a: No. They help you talk, but if you're going through a real crisis, a couples counsellor or therapist will be much more useful. Nothing stops you from using these questions as well, though.
